companyDescription: Direct-to-smartphone satellite broadband · BlueBird constellation now 13 birds up, production through satellite 42 — building a space-based cellular network standard phones can already use
priceNote: Live price Aug 13 07:49, +3.74% today. Prior report (Aug 4) used $63.52 — +17.0% drift in 9 days, the largest on the visible board, which is what triggered this refresh. Both of that report's near catalysts have since fired successfully.
summary: Both near-term catalysts from the last report landed, and landed well. BlueBird 11/12/13 launched successfully on Aug 5 from Cape Canaveral aboard a Falcon 9 — the largest communications arrays ever put in low Earth orbit, over 3x the size of Block 1, supporting peak rates near 200 Mbps direct to unmodified smartphones. Q2 2026 revenue came in at $31.5M (mostly gateway deliveries) with full-year guidance reaffirmed at $150-200M, and manufacturing has advanced through satellite 42. Consensus sits at $83.32 against $74.31 — about +12%, with upgrade targets running to $115. The execution risk that dominated this thesis a year ago has measurably decreased; what remains is a valuation risk, since a $28.8B market cap is already paying for a constellation that isn't finished and revenue that is still nine figures away from the multiple.

catalystSpot.preRunupTiming: 1-2 สัปดาห์ก่อน launch

postWin.note: Range is genuinely wide because launch significance varies enormously. ASTS's own BlueBird 1 launch (Apr 2024) produced +100% because it proved the concept; incremental launches into an existing constellation are worth far less, which is why the Aug 5 launch moved the stock ~17% rather than double.

postLose.note: For ASTS the realistic downside catalyst is financing, not launch failure: the Jul 2026 $1.15B convertible offering took the stock down 13% after hours. A launch anomaly would be worse.

spotSizing.reason: Held at 3%. Execution risk genuinely fell with a successful launch and reaffirmed guidance, but that is offset by paying 17% more than the last report and sitting above the fair-value estimate. The satellite_launch leader status does not justify sizing up (n=8, guardrail is explicit).
